content:
Since all Carlson jars weigh at least \(5k\), we need
\[
117k - 5k(n-1) \ge 5k
\]
which simplifies to
\[
5kn \le 117k \quad\Rightarrow\quad n \le \frac{117}{5}=23.4.
\]
Thus \(n \le 23\).

This maximum is attainable: take \(k=1\), Carlson has 22 jars weighing \(5\) pounds and one jar weighing \(7\) pounds. Total is \(117\), Baby has \(9\). Giving one \(5\)-pound jar leaves Carlson with \(112\) and Baby with \(14\), and \(112=8\cdot 14\).

\[
\boxed{23}
\]
